newsitem.title: LEBANON: Palestinian convicted in Kuwait embassy blast.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian convicted in Kuwait embassy blast.

text.p: A Lebanese military court has sentenced a former Palestinian guerrilla in absentia to life in prison for lobbing a bomb into the Kuwaiti embassy in Beirut and the attempted bombing of the Kuwaiti Airlines office in 1993.
The court on Friday night sentenced Mohammad Hillal, a 48-year-old former official of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP), to life in prison with hard labour for the attacks.
The indictment that charged Hillal had said that he was instructed by the Iraqi embassy to carry out the attacks.

Hillal was found guilty of lobbing a bomb into the embassy compound in Beirut in March 1993 -- the blast broke windows but caused no casualties -- and of planting a bomb in front of the Kuwaiti Airlines office in the capital the following August.
Lebanese police defused an eight-kg (18-pound) bomb in front of the airlines office on August 23, 1993, the eve of a visit to Lebanon by the emir of Kuwait Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmed al-Sabah.
Iraqi sympathisers tossed dynamite sticks at the Kuwait Airlines office in Beirut during the buildup to the expulsion of invading Iraqi forces from Kuwait in 1991 by a U.S.-led force.
Lebanon supported but did not contribute troops to the multinational coalition.
